metadata.scenario_context: A group of environmentalists from different countries are planning a global event to advocate for climate change. They decided to have a preparatory meeting in June to present their individual campaign strategies

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from France disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Philippines agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Proposes to have the meeting on June 20,
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion around finalizing the date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Julia
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Tesfaye, I was thinking... what do you think about having our preparatory meeting on June 20? It seems like a good date to present our campaign strategies.  

Also, do you think it’s common for people to discuss the appropriateness of government actions? Because I feel like in France, we really don’t have much say in what our government does…
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Tesfaye
shared_prefix.message:
June 20... Sounds fine. We need to move forward with it. 

As for discussing government actions, well, in the Philippines, it’s tough. We rarely have a say in what happens. It's like shouting into a void. It's frustrating when our voices get lost like that. But I guess it varies by country...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Julia
shared_prefix.message: I completely understand what you’re saying, Tesfaye. It’s tough when our voices feel unheard. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things — wanting to be heard, to make a difference. It’s a small world after all, and regardless of where we come from, we share that basic need to communicate. So, I think it’s important we keep pushing for our voices to be recognized, no matter where we are.
